correctness.rationale: The connected weighted-Laplacian inverse-trace objective has a strictly positive second variation for any nonzero edge perturbation. Unique unrestricted optimality forces rotation-invariant classes. Fourier decomposition yields the exact objective; first and second spectral moments establish the sharp activation price and its quadratic onset. Uniform Fourier sums and derivative bracketing prove the large-n limit and critical window. Independent exact symbolic and randomly asymmetric computational checks corroborate, without replacing, these infinite arguments.

value.rationale: An exact topology-switch threshold determines when the marginal price of redundant rim links makes every one of them uneconomic, a natural optimal-network-design decision. The quadratic advantage near the transition and the n^{-1} critical-window scaling quantify structurally meaningful finite-size effects that distinguish finite wheel design from its large-network limit. These are motivated quantities independent of the numerical verification exercise.
